title: Camera-to-photo pipeline
description: Take a phone camera frame (YUV_420_888 planes), downgrade it to camcorder resolution, run bend -> date stamp -> VHS -> dither -> viewfinder overlay, and make the saved photo exactly what the viewfinder showed.

clauses.text: The phone's camera image is cropped to 4:3, rotated upright and averaged down to the chosen low resolution (camcorder 320x240, or Game Boy Camera 128x112).
clauses.observable_by: a test named "camera frames are downsampled upright" passes

clauses.text: The photo you take is exactly the frame the viewfinder showed - overlay, bends and all - just scaled up with hard pixel edges.
clauses.observable_by: a test named "photo is the viewfinder frame scaled up" passes

clauses.text: With dither on, the whole photo, overlay included, uses only the palette's colours; with bend on, the picture differs from bend off.
clauses.observable_by: a test named "filters toggle independently" passes

clauses.text: The full chain with everything switched on runs fast enough for a live viewfinder (well under one frame at 30 fps on a desktop JVM, leaving headroom for a phone).
clauses.observable_by: a test named "full chain is fast enough for live preview" passes

cases.description: synthetic Y/U/V planes with a marker in one corner, at rotations 0/90/180/270, interleaved chroma (pixelStride 2), row padding filled with bright garbage that must never be sampled, and a 40/200 checkerboard that must box-average to mid-grey
capture output at scale k equals each viewfinder pixel repeated k x k
dither on -> only palette colours; bend on -> differs from bend off

median of 15 runs at 320x240 with all effects on, after warm-up, under 20 ms - declared guard: a do-nothing stub is trivially fast, so this can never be observed red; it must keep holding once the real chain exists
